speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for National Development whether the Ministry will consider making it mandatory for commercial and residential buildings to install and operate solar panels on their roofs, with exceptions granted only on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, there are constraints that limit this wide-scale deployment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, there are competing uses for roof spaces, such as rooftop greenery, as well as facilities, such as water tanks, lift machine rooms and antennas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The public sector takes the lead by aggregating demand for solar deployment across Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Ministry monitoring the experience of other countries in the world that are making this mandatory, at least for some categories of buildings?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe this is either being considered or has already been implemented in some cities in America, India and France.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, will the Ministry be monitoring their experience and try to draw some lessons when reviewing this at some future point in time?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it would not have been able to Page: 46 fulfil the total needs of the country.
